correctness.rationale: For b≥2,c≥0, sum-incidence edges have weights s_j=b^j+c; unions of two weight matchings are forests, and s_j>2s_{j-1} excludes any higher-weight edge on a cycle below first threshold. At c≥b(b-2), explicit 2b+2 cycle uses the first three levels. In intermediate band b≥3, the highest-weight obstruction excludes j≥3; eligible s_2 edges have distinct left residues modulo d=b-1, so a component has at most one, and its two-matching endpoint path has precisely 2b+1 edges. At c≥b²-b-1 explicit six-cycle exists; pair-sum uniqueness for b powers forbids 4-cycles. b=2 intermediate singleton checked separately. Independent BFS computed three-level graph girth for 63 (b,c) pairs b=2..6 and c<min(17,b²): every case matched ∞/2b+2/6. The infinite result rests on highest-edge proof; binary-word corollary uses published forest characterization.

evidence: Published October 25 statement proves forest iff c<b(b-2) and constructs 2b+2 cycle above; no lower bound ruling out smaller cycles. The general three-spike rank formula counts cycles but does not directly bound girth for infinite all-weight support.
